editorial.headline: Water Infrastructure Works: Open Nationally, Available for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the construction, maintenance and repair of civil water infrastructure and related works, open to foreign investment nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity covers civil water-infrastructure works and comparable civil works not otherwise captured within the classification. Its scope extends across the full working life of that infrastructure: construction, maintenance and repair. That framing is broad, but it is not vague. The activity is defined by its relationship to civil water infrastructure and related works, rather than by a single phase of delivery. New construction and later care for the same class of civil asset can therefore sit within one stated field of work.

The registration is relevant to an enterprise whose stated work includes building, maintaining or repairing civil water infrastructure and the related civil works described by the scope. It is open at every listed scale: micro, small, medium and large. That breadth matters because the defined activity is available to smaller and growing operators as well as larger enterprises; the record does not confine it to one business size. Editorially, it is a construction activity with a complete operational arc: create the infrastructure, maintain it, and repair it when needed.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is open. The record sets maximum foreign ownership at 100%, with Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the cited source. For a foreign-owned company, the central point is straightforward: the national ceiling does not require the foreign stake to stop below full ownership. This is the national reference point for the activity, and it aligns directly with the stated open status.

Bali does not turn that national opening into a prohibition. This activity is not blocked for PMA registration there, and its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason is specific: at the large scale, its OSS risk is medium-high/high, placing it outside Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium for PMA on all low and medium-low risk KBLI. The honest Bali conclusion is therefore clean: the activity remains available for PMA registration in Bali, while the national maximum foreign ownership remains 100%.
